challenges.says: The criterion about a stored comment appearing in the section has an empty citation and gives no reason, although businessrule-77000026808397550095 states exactly that (comment included only when one is stored), so it should cite it.

The last criterion joins two unrelated behaviours (comment escaping of backslashes and line breaks, and copying a selected line with Ctrl+C) with 'Also:', so a tester cannot pass or fail each alone; each belongs in its own criterion.

The option-value criterion drops parts of businessrule-10913365400690794412: text is written with no escaping so text holding a quote or line break cannot be read back, and quotes inside list-of-text items are doubled.

The comment-escaping criterion drops the consequence stated in businessrule-78281155676242942940 (a lone line feed or carriage return splits the comment over two script lines and corrupts it when read back), which is the point of the rule.

The criterion on choice names ('named as the file that defines the policy names it') is hard for a product owner to follow; it should say that choice names come from the definitions file that defines the policy.
